x: Derek Hurd was on this stage for Belgrave, but has not been running long enough yet to match this class of opposition. He is young enough to be eligible for next year's race so, with 12 months of conscientious training, could well be to the fore next time.

However, we had played our best cards, and Derek Hurd was left with the unenviable task of facing some hot opposition on the last stage. Despite Derek's hard fight we had to be content with 10th position

In the Youths, Adrian Major, Ron Hayes, Bill Bruce and more recently Derek Hurd have shown considerable potential and if they maintain their progress they could well be strengthening the senior ranks in a few years time.
Adrian Major also had a fine run to finish 10th and was ably supported by Ron Hayes (19th) and Derek Hurd (27th) to give us a comfortable 3rd place.
John was well backed up by Adrian Major, 39th,Derek Hurd 54th, and Ron Hayes 75th - the team did wel[illegible] to take 6th place with 186 points.

Adrian Major had a good run to finish 62nd and Ron Hayes produced his usual sound performance to be our 3rd man. Derek Hurd completed our scoring four. The team ran well, and their 12th place out of the 66 team that closed in deserves high praise.
Derek Hurd carried the baton first for us but suffered towards the handover and set Bicourt off in 6th position. By this time the Mitcham 1st quartet were in the lead and continued to make ground.

I was very pleased indeed to see two of our boys back again fit and well after a long absence - Ron Hayes and Derek Hurd.Ron has recovered from a serious illness,and tells me that he has now resumed full time work.

Church and Badgery have already made names for themselves in the Youth athletics world and it is certain that Adrian is on the brink of making his also. Derek Hurd ran unexpectedly well to finish 10th, and has considerable potential.

Great backing by Derek Hurd (who seems to be finding his old form) and quarter-miler Philip Smith (he could never have dreamed of winning his first County medal in a cross country race) ensured us of a suprise 2nd place in the team event.
Youth John Kelly was 2nd after running the entire race on his own, followed home three-quarters of a minute later by Phil Smith who ran extremely well to beat Derek Hurd.
Jim Heathfield put in some useful running to take the handicap from Jim Rimmer ( a man to watch) who was a good second. Handicap Result: 1.J.Heathfield 26:13, 2.J.Rimmer 26:21, 3.D.Hurd 26:38
